# Whether the conversation state this build composes onto cursor's blob channel
# reaches the model — whether a second turn remembers the first — and what the
# server fetches of it.
#
# The recording W3's gate reads (.omc/plans/2026-09-07-cursor-history-blobs.md,
# W2; AC-13). Two live turns against api2.cursor.sh, both run by the user
# through `!` — no lane and no lead ran one, and nothing here was read out of
# auth.json. What the wire itself said is in the run's own log at `-v`; the
# line numbers below are that file's. The log was grepped for the three
# credential markers the lane charter names (a bearer prefix, a key prefix, a
# JWT header) before a line of this was written: zero hits over 7,015 lines.
#
# Recorded by: the shipped wire's own debug lines, no spike scaffolding this
#              time — history.rs's two lines at the end of `blobs` (:503,
#              :522: counts, then sorted id prefixes with sizes) and
#              request.rs's three in `kv_answer` (:595 get, :613 set, :631 a
#              set that replaced held bytes). Line numbers are 4a9ac1d's.
# Build:  ganja-code 0.1.0; ./target/release/ganja rebuilt from 4a9ac1d (W1,
#         "provider: carry the conversation on cursor's blob channel").
# Date:   2026-09-06, 18:16:37 - 18:17:29 UTC (2026-09-07 03:16 - 03:17 JST;
#         the log file is named by the local date).
# Log:    ~/.local/share/ganja/log/ganja.2026-09-07.log, 7,015 lines; the two
#         runs are :6810-:6921 and :6922-:7015, the last 206.
# Server: api2.cursor.sh. This client identified as cli-2026.01.09-231024f
#         (cursor.rs:138, sent as x-cursor-client-version at :557), the
#         constant cursor.rs has always sent.
# Model:  GANJA_MODEL unset on both runs, so the turn ran under cursor's
#         server-side `default` (Auto). Which model that resolved to is decided
#         server-side and is not observable from this client. The config's
#         `effort = "xhigh"` was dropped at adoption (:6816, :6930) because
#         `default` carries no effort ladder.
#
# What the wire carried that no request before 4a9ac1d did: on the second run,
# AgentRunRequest.conversation_state{root_prompt_messages_json = 6 ids,
# turns = 1 id}, every id the sha256 of bytes seeded into the Run's blob store
# before the stream opened, and AgentRunRequest.conversation_id on BOTH runs —
# derived from the first message's own id, so the same value on both, by
# construction (history.rs `derived`; the log never prints it).
#
# NO CONNECT ERROR OF ANY KIND WAS PRODUCED BY EITHER RUN. No `code`, no
# `message`, no EndStream error frame, no `Blob not found`, no
# `invalid_argument`, no ProviderEvent::Failed. The one line in the window
# that a case-insensitive grep for "failed" finds is :6851, a bridged `read`
# whose *tool* outcome was `failed` (file not found) — a tool result the model
# read, not a wire failure. The plan asks for every error code and message
# verbatim; the honest verbatim record is that there were none.
#
# This directory's rule holds here: no token, no tool-argument value and no
# reply text. What the user's terminal printed — the two replies — is
# described, never quoted; the lane charter under .omc/handoffs/ holds the
# stdout for whoever needs the exact bytes.

== probe 1 ==

== the runs ==
# One line per run: the command as the user ran it (GANJA_PROVIDER=cursor,
# nothing else set), the log window, and the run's turn — composition line
# to `step_completed (17)`.
R1  run -v "Remember the code word PELICAN-7. Reply with OK and nothing else."
                                     log :6810-:6921   turn :6819-:6912  (15.64 s)
R2  run -v --continue "What code word did I ask you to remember, and what is
    the current working directory? One line."
                                     log :6922-:7015   turn :6932-:7006  (9.22 s)

# Both runs ended by printing a reply and exiting; neither emitted a
# ProviderEvent::Failed. The wire logs no line for a clean EndStream and none
# for the run request's send, so "the turn completed" here means: a reply was
# printed, `step_completed (17)` was decoded (:6912, :7006), the process
# exited, and no failure was reported.

# R1's turn was not the no-call turn the plan's procedure assumed (A-M2: "turn
# 1 makes no call"). The model called three of ganja's tools through the
# declared roster, every one arriving as `mcp_args` and bridged (D552):
#
#   :6848  bridging an exec  exec=1 kind="mcp_args" tool="read"
#   :6851  answering a bridged exec  exec=1 tool="read"  outcome="failed"
#   :6853  bridging an exec  exec=2 kind="mcp_args" tool="glob"
#   :6859  answering a bridged exec  exec=2 tool="glob"  outcome="ran"
#   :6885  bridging an exec  exec=3 kind="mcp_args" tool="bash"
#   :6889  answering a bridged exec  exec=3 tool="bash"  outcome="refused"
#
# (the `read` answered file-not-found; the `glob` ran and matched nothing; the
# `bash` was auto-rejected, as a headless run without --auto rejects every
# dialog). The reply then printed the one word the prompt asked for. So R2's
# history carried an assistant entry with three `[Tool Call]` paragraphs and
# three result entries — two `[Tool Result (error)]`, one `[Tool Result]` —
# and the state below is larger than the plan's `entries = 3` by exactly
# those. See "incidental": this pre-measures W3's P3.
#
# R2's turn made one call, `bash` (:6961, exec=1, kind="mcp_args"), refused
# the same way (:6967 outcome="refused"), and answered anyway.

== P1 — does the composed history reach the model ==
VERDICT: YES

The second reply named the code word the first prompt asked the model to
remember, in one line beside the working directory. Nothing in R2's own
prompt carries the word; the only channel it could have reached the model by
is the state below.

R2's composition, :6932-:6933:

  :6932  composed the conversation state provider="cursor" entries=6 turns=1
         blobs=12 bytes=171566 clamped_calls=0 action="user"
  :6933  the composed blob ids provider="cursor" ids=[
           "08dfcb1a9e5054ba=86",   "24551d6ffef6a9a4=633",  "449d69fc21ec4914=173",
           "50b657d2779825dc=549",  "5fab41de977ff5dd=198",  "88a3603a48ff45bc=150",
           "9b2c0716baa430d1=136",  "a01d5bda822aaef7=32",   "c5ab3958edfbbe51=169304",
           "e0e4ac3d0f3ef169=82",   "f31f7f6c3ce521d5=118",  "fdebda7208d1cfd0=105" ]

entries=6 is the system head, R1's user message, R1's assistant entry (its
text and three `[Tool Call]` paragraphs), and three result entries; turns=1
is R1's one turn; blobs=12 is 6 root JSON entries + 1 UserMessage + 4
ConversationSteps + 1 ConversationTurn, and the twelve sizes sum to 171,566.

The server's gets, :6935-:6941 — seven, all within 48 µs of one another
(18:17:21.665657Z - .665705Z: one batch), 0.98 s after the composition line,
before any set, and every one answered found:

  :6935  answering the server's kv get blob="449d69fc21ec4914" found=173
  :6936  answering the server's kv get blob="9b2c0716baa430d1" found=136
  :6937  answering the server's kv get blob="c5ab3958edfbbe51" found=169304
  :6938  answering the server's kv get blob="f31f7f6c3ce521d5" found=118
  :6939  answering the server's kv get blob="24551d6ffef6a9a4" found=633
  :6940  answering the server's kv get blob="5fab41de977ff5dd" found=198
  :6941  answering the server's kv get blob="e0e4ac3d0f3ef169" found=82

(`found=<n>` is tracing's rendering of `Some(n)`; a miss would print the line
with no `found` field at all, and no such line exists in the window.)

Which composed ids were fetched and which were not. The log carries prefixes
and sizes only, but the twelve sizes decompose exactly against the shapes
history.rs builds (JSON frame 53 bytes for a `user` root entry, 58 for an
`assistant` one; every proto field here is number 1 or 2, so a 1-byte tag
plus a length):

  root[0]  c5ab3958edfbbe51  169304  system head, the one six-figure blob   FETCHED :6937
  root[1]  f31f7f6c3ce521d5     118  user: 53 + the 65-byte prompt           FETCHED :6938
  root[2]  24551d6ffef6a9a4     633  assistant text + 3 [Tool Call]s         FETCHED :6939
  root[3]  5fab41de977ff5dd     198  [Tool Result (error)] read: 53+144+1    FETCHED :6940
  root[4]  e0e4ac3d0f3ef169      82  [Tool Result] glob: 53+28+1 (the 28 is
                                     the marker, a newline, and glob.rs:96's
                                     own "No files found")                   FETCHED :6941
  root[5]  9b2c0716baa430d1     136  [Tool Result (error)] bash: 53+82+1
                                     (the 82: marker, newline, the 60-byte
                                     refusal sentence permission_text renders) FETCHED :6936
  turns[0] 449d69fc21ec4914     173  ConversationTurn: 1+2+(5 × (1+1+32)) —
                                     one user_message id and four step ids    FETCHED :6935
  turn.user_message
           fdebda7208d1cfd0     105  UserMessage: (1+1+65 text) +
                                     (1+1+36 derived message_id)             not fetched
  step[0]  50b657d2779825dc     549  the assistant text in proto framing
                                     (by elimination: 633 is the same text
                                     JSON-escaped, +58 frame)                not fetched
  step[1]  88a3603a48ff45bc     150  read result: 1+2+(1+2+144)              not fetched
  step[2]  a01d5bda822aaef7      32  glob result: 1+1+(1+1+28)               not fetched
  step[3]  08dfcb1a9e5054ba      86  bash result: 1+1+(1+1+82)               not fetched

Fetched: all six root entries (170,471 bytes) and the ConversationTurn
wrapper (173). Not fetched: the five blobs only that wrapper names — the
turn's user_message and its four steps (922 bytes). This is the reference's
own claim (`proxy.ts:744-750`: the server builds the prompt from
`root_prompt_messages_json`, not from `turns[]`) observed from the client
side, with one addition the reference does not state: the server does
dereference the turn *wrapper* — it just never follows the ids inside it. So
on this recording a divergence in the model's memory would trace to the root
and nowhere else, which is what history.rs's module doc predicted.

Fetch order was turns[0], root[5], root[0], root[1], root[2], root[3],
root[4] — the last root entry ahead of the first, in one batch. One sample;
nothing here says the order is stable.

Reading checklist (C-M5, C-M1'):

  * A get for an id this build never minted: NO. All seven gets name ids in
    the :6933 listing, and no get went unanswered-found. Five composed ids
    were never asked for; no asked-for id was uncomposed.

  * Either `message_id` echoed anywhere visible: NOT DETERMINABLE FROM THE
    LOG. This build prints neither id it minted — the history blob's derived
    one nor the action's random one (request.rs:230 `fresh_id`) — and a
    case-sensitive grep of the window for `message_id` and `conversation_id`
    returns nothing. The only server-minted ids the log shows are the tool
    call ids on the `bridging an exec` lines, shaped `call-<v4 uuid>-<n>`
    over `fc_<hex>_<n>`: R1's step-1 execs (:6848, :6853) share one uuid with
    indices -0/-1 and its step-2 exec (:6885) carries a different uuid with
    -2, so those are per-step mints of the server's own — a Run carries
    exactly one action message_id, and two distinct uuids appeared inside
    one Run. Whether one of them coincides with the id this client sent
    cannot be checked without the client printing it.

  * Anything in R2 attributable to `conversation_id`: NOTHING SEPARABLE.
    Both runs carried one — the same derived value — so the presence of the
    field is not a variable between them. R2 differs from R1 in exactly the
    ways the supplied state predicts (seven gets where R1 had none; a
    shorter turn with one call where R1 had three) and in one way it does
    not: R1's server set a 190,884-byte blob at :6826, 2.7 s in, and R2's
    server set nothing larger than 3,735 bytes (:7004) in the whole run.
    That could be the server declining to write its own head because the
    client supplied a root, or the server recognizing a conversation_id it
    had seen 43 s earlier; one recording cannot tell those apart.

== P1b — does the working directory arrive (smoke, not a discriminator) ==
VERDICT: YES — and it proves only "at least one channel"

The reply's second half was the checkout's absolute path, which is what the
system prompt's `<env>` block carries. It did not come from a tool: the one
thing the model tried, `bash` (:6961), was refused (:6967), and the reply
was printed anyway.

Why this settles nothing about which channel: the plan's own sentence — "Both
channels carry the *same* string (`cloud_rule` is `request.system` at
`request.rs:257`; the head is the same `request.system`), so a correct
directory proves only that the system prompt reached the model by **at least
one** channel; it cannot say which, and doubling is not observable from this
side at all." At 4a9ac1d that line is request.rs:301, not :257 — the plan's
number predates W1's edits to the file. On R1 there was no head (entries=0,
:6819: "the system head appears only beside history"), so R1's directory
could only have come from `cloud_rule`; on R2 both channels carried it.

== P2 — every get found, no error frame, and what the fetch cost ==
VERDICT: YES

Every get for a composed id was found (the seven lines above). No `Blob not
found`, no `invalid_argument`, no EndStream error, no Failed event in either
run's window; `a server set replaced bytes this run already held` (the :631
line, which would name a differing re-set of a held id) appears zero times
in the window and zero times in the whole 7,015-line log.

Gets before the first model output, and the wall time to it. This build logs
no line for a text delta (decode.rs:346-347 emits the event silently; only
thinking deltas are logged, :357) and none for the run request's send, so the
two ends measurable here are the composition line — logged inside
`run_message`'s assembly, immediately before the send — and the first
`thinking delta`. The number is therefore an upper bound on send-to-first-
thinking, and the first *text* delta is later by an amount the log does not
show.

  R2  composition :6932 18:17:20.681416Z
      gets        :6935-:6941 at +0.984 s (7, all found, 170,644 bytes served)
      sets        :6945-:6947 at +1.964 s (3: 2262, 260, 225)
      first thinking delta :6948 18:17:24.259983Z    = +3.579 s
      gets before that delta: 7   sets before it: 3

  R1  composition :6819 18:16:37.810929Z
      gets        none
      sets        :6825 at +2.012 s (2262), :6826-:6828 at +2.663 s
                  (190884, 90, 196)
      first thinking delta :6829 18:16:45.071990Z    = +7.261 s
      gets before that delta: 0   sets before it: 4

Read carefully: the run that fetched 171 KB of state reached its first
thinking 3.7 s *sooner* than the run that fetched nothing. One sample per
arm, one model, one afternoon — this is not a measurement of the fetch's
cost, and the ADR's expiry clause should read it as "the seven gets and
their 170 KB did not push TTFT past the empty-state run's own", not as a
saving. What the two numbers do bound: the batch of seven gets was issued
and answered within one second of the request going out, and the model was
producing 1.6 s after the server's first set.

== P4-pre — the checkpoint arm ==
VERDICT: ARRIVES, on both runs: 12 times, n from 558 to 7465

`unmodelled server-message fields provider="cursor" fields=[(3, n)]`:

  R1  :6862 (3, 7465)  :6871 (3, 558)   :6890 (3, 2578)  :6897 (3, 626)
      :6909 (3, 1882)  :6911 (3, 660)   :6913 (3, 660)                   7 arrivals
  R2  :6968 (3, 3269)  :6975 (3, 683)   :7003 (3, 4499)  :7005 (3, 717)
      :7007 (3, 717)                                                    5 arrivals

Placement, the same on both runs: one arrives after each tool_call_completed
or kv-set burst, and the run's last two are a pair of identical size that
brackets `step_completed (17)` (:6912 between the two 660s; :7006 between the
two 717s). The largest, 7465 at :6862, followed R1's first two bridged execs.
Only the size is seen; the arm is not decoded.

== what this cannot measure ==

1. One seat, one account, one model (`default`/Auto), one client version,
   one afternoon, one turn of history. Nothing here says what a named model,
   a different tier, or a later server does — nor what a *longer* history
   does: R2 named one turn (12 blobs); a session of ten turns, or one whose
   history has been re-rooted by compaction, is unmeasured.

2. Head doubling is not observable from this side. R2 carried
   `request.system` twice — as root[0] and as `cloud_rule` — and a model
   that reads both, either, or one twice leaves the same trace here. The
   P1b section says why the directory cannot discriminate.

3. Server-side use of `conversation_id` is not observable. Both runs sent
   the same derived value; nothing came back that names it, and the one
   behavioural difference not explained by the supplied state (the 190 KB
   set on R1 only) has two candidate causes this recording cannot separate.

4. Nothing about a bridged (paused) Run's *history* — a step that resumes
   from `Action::Resume` with the assistant's message last. Every request
   here was `action="user"`; the Resume arm was never sent. That is probe
   2's.

5. Whether the five unfetched blobs are *never* read, or merely were not
   read on this turn. One recording of one server: the turn's user_message
   and steps were not dereferenced here, which matches the reference's
   claim, and does not prove the server has no path that would.

6. The `[Tool Call]` input clamp: `clamped_calls=0` on every composition,
   because no call's input reached 8 KiB. The elision text and the count are
   unit-tested, not live-measured.

7. First-*text*-delta timing, the run request's send instant, and the clean
   EndStream: none has a log line in this build, so every timing above is
   composition-to-first-thinking and "the turn completed" is inferred from
   the printed reply, the decoded step_completed and the clean exit.

8. What the checkpoint arm (3, n) carries: only its byte count reaches the
   log, and whether it is a checkpoint at all is the plan's naming, not a
   decoded fact.

== incidental, and worth knowing before W3 ==

* `[Tool Call]` and `[Tool Result …]` text was sent and accepted a wave
  early. Because R1's model called three tools, R2's request was the first
  this build has ever sent carrying an assistant root entry with `[Tool
  Call]` paragraphs (root[2], 633 bytes) and both result flavours (root[3]
  and root[5] as `(error)`, root[4] plain) — and the reply was correct. W3's
  P3 was to be the first measurement of that shape; it is pre-measured here
  for the un-paused case. The plan's A-M2 attribution premise ("It carries
  no `[Tool Call]` text") did not hold on this recording; since P1 passed,
  nothing needed attributing.

* Every exec on both runs arrived as `mcp_args` — the model reached ganja's
  `read`, `glob` and `bash` by the names the roster declared, never through
  a native kind redirected (D552's second door). Each hold was short: 106 ms
  (:6850→:6851), 66 ms (:6858→:6859), 110 ms (:6888→:6889), 70 ms
  (:6966→:6967).

* `ganja run` still constructs the cursor wire twice per invocation (the
  reference probe's first incidental). Here it shows as a second
  composition with `entries=0` at :6918 and :7012, at process teardown
  after step_completed — the title/summary one-shot — followed by no get
  and no set: composed and logged, never sent.

* The first kv set of each run is the same blob at the same size:
  `a3b587832706c9c6` size=2262 at :6825 and :6945. The server's set ids are
  deterministic across processes for at least that one blob.

* R1's server set a 190,884-byte blob (:6826) before its first delta — the
  reference probe saw one of that order on its R5 (185,582 bytes); R2's
  server never set anything above 3,735 bytes. Two candidate causes, above;
  one recording.

* kv sets in the window: 24 on R1, 15 on R2, 39 in all. (148 is the whole
  day's log, every session since 00:00 local.)

* The MCP servers a session dials at startup (context7 at :6942, the gemini
  plugin at :6944) connected *after* the seven gets had been answered
  (:6935-:6941). They did not gate the run request.

* Beside the `partial_tool_call (7)`, `tool_call_started (2)` and
  `tool_call_completed (3)` arms this build skips, every one of those lines
  also names an unmodelled `field 25` on the update (:6844, :6846, :6847,
  :6852, :6860, …). Unchanged from before W1; noted because a reader of
  this log will see it beside every tool call.

== probe 2 ==
# Whether a bridged Run whose hold outlived the idle bound is recovered — the
# next request reopening a Run over the composed conversation under
# `resume_action` — and whether the tool that paused it runs exactly once.
#
# The recording W4's gate reads (.omc/plans/2026-09-07-cursor-history-blobs.md,
# W3 "Probe 2"; AC-20). One live turn in the TUI against api2.cursor.sh, run
# by the user through `!` — no lane and no lead ran one, and nothing here was
# read out of auth.json. The same three credential markers were grepped for
# before a line of this was written: zero hits over the 53-line window the
# charter named, and zero over the whole 7,264-line file.
#
# Recorded by: the shipped wire's own lines, no scaffolding — bridge.rs's two
#              (:349 holding, :378 dropping), cursor.rs's INFO at :447
#              (recovering) and its bridging line at :1040, history.rs's two
#              (:511, :522), request.rs's kv pair (:599 get, :617 set) and
#              decode.rs's three (:341 unmodelled fields, :357 thinking, :385
#              skipped arms). Line numbers are d8fc38e's.
# Build:  ganja-code 0.1.0; ./target/release/ganja rebuilt from d8fc38e (W3,
#         "provider,testkit,core: recover a cursor turn whose held Run is
#         gone, once").
# Date:   2026-09-06, 18:59:08 - 19:11:11 UTC (2026-09-07 03:59 - 04:11 JST).
# Log:    the same file, 7,264 lines at writing; the session is :7016-:7264,
#         the last 249. The charter's window, :7039-:7091, is not a session
#         boundary: :7016-:7038 are the session's startup, :7039-:7085 the
#         turn's wire lines, and :7086-:7264 the title one-shot's own Run.
# Server: api2.cursor.sh; the client version string probe 1 names, unchanged.
# Model:  GANJA_MODEL unset, so `default` (Auto) again; the config's effort
#         dropped at adoption (:7025). Which model Auto resolved to on each of
#         the three Runs is server-side and not observable here.
# Frontend: the TUI, where probe 1 was `ganja run`. Two differences follow
#         from that and are named where they show: the newest user message
#         carries the engine's request-only text (the session's five MCP
#         tools were deferred at threshold=0, :7034-:7037, where probe 1's
#         headless runs built their requests before any MCP server had
#         connected), and the title one-shot is sent rather than composed at
#         teardown.
#
# What the wire carried that no request before d8fc38e did: a run request
# under `resume_action` (request.rs:240-241) — the first this build has ever
# sent to the server. Every earlier live request, probe 1's included, was
# `action="user"`; the Resume arm had only ever gone to the testkit's mock.
# Its state carried an assistant root entry that is one `[Tool Call]`
# paragraph and nothing else, and a `[Tool Result]` entry for a call the
# *server* had asked for as an exec and never got an answer to on the body
# it asked on.
#
# NO CONNECT ERROR OF ANY KIND WAS PRODUCED. No `code`, no `message`, no
# EndStream error frame, no `Blob not found`, no `invalid_argument`, no
# ProviderEvent::Failed, no cap sentence ("already reopened once": zero
# lines), and a case-insensitive grep of the session for "failed" and
# "error" returns nothing at all — not even probe 1's tool-outcome line,
# since the one tool here ran.
#
# This directory's rule holds: no token, no tool-argument value (the plan's
# 82-byte command is referred to by its length), no thinking text. The reply
# was the single character `1` — P3's measurement, which the plan's own text
# names — and it is stated as that rather than quoted as prose.

== the run ==
# One session, one prompt — the plan's two lines, 167 bytes as the composer
# took them (:7033) — three Runs on the wire, one turn. `A` is the Run the
# tool call paused, `B` the Run the recovery opened, `C` the title one-shot.

  session      :7016-:7264  18:59:08.59Z - 19:11:11.30Z              (722.72 s)
  T1 the turn  :7032-:7085  Enter 18:59:26.90Z - step_completed
                            19:11:07.97Z                             (701.08 s)
    A paused   :7039-:7059  composition 18:59:27.14Z, held 18:59:35.67Z,
                            dropped 19:09:35.68Z
    B recovery :7060-:7085  recovery 19:10:59.20Z - step_completed
                            19:11:07.97Z                               (8.77 s)
  C one-shot   :7086-:7264  composition 19:11:08.01Z - step_completed
                            19:11:11.30Z                               (3.29 s)

# A, line by line. entries=0 is the first-turn shape probe 1's R1 had (the
# head appears only beside history); the prompt rode the action inline.

  :7039  composed the conversation state entries=0 turns=0 blobs=0 bytes=0
         clamped_calls=0 action="user"                    18:59:27.141315Z
  :7041  kv set 2260                                      +1.916 s
  :7042  kv set 191609   :7043 90   :7044 1402            +2.548 s
  :7045  first thinking delta (24; :7047 24, :7049 20 — 68 bytes, the

== P3 — the recovery, over the composed history, and the tool ran once ==
VERDICT: YES

The two lines, verbatim (neither carries a secret):

  :7059  2026-09-06T19:09:35.675792Z DEBUG ganja_provider::provider::cursor::bridge: dropping a held run provider="cursor" reason=Idle
  :7060  2026-09-06T19:10:59.203014Z  INFO ganja_provider::provider::cursor: recovering a cursor turn on a fresh run provider="cursor" why=this turn is answering a cursor tool call, but the run that asked for it is gone: it was not resumed within the idle bound; reopening a run over the composed conversation

What each proves.

  * The drop is the shipped path at the shipped bound. `reason=Idle` is
    `keep()`'s third arm (bridge.rs:566), 600.006 s after the hold against
    IDLE_BOUND = 600 s (bridge.rs:130); the 6 ms is the select's own
    scheduling. It is `Idle` and not `Closed`, and that is a measurement:
    `Closed` is returned on the first heartbeat whose send fails
    (bridge.rs:567-570), so every one of the ~120 beats sent on that body
    over ten minutes succeeded — the server, or at least the connection
    under it, tolerated a beating held body for the whole 600 s. The D552
    recording bounded that from below at 25 s (bridge.rs:25-27); this one
    bounds it at 600 s. Nothing here says where the ceiling is, nor
    whether a resume written to that body at 599 s would have been read.

  * The recovery keyed to the dropped Run. The sentence's clause — "it was
    not resumed within the idle bound" — is `Reason::Idle`'s spelling
    (bridge.rs:211), and `because(key)` reads it from the ring's entry for
    the request's own key; a request that keyed elsewhere would have
    recovered with no clause. So `(model, messages[turn_start].id)` came
    out the same on the request that answered the dialog as on the one
    the hold was taken under.

  * The request went out under `resume_action`. :7061 says
    `action="resume"`, which is `entries()`'s second arm (history.rs:225 —
    the request's last message is the assistant's) and reaches the wire as
    `ConversationAction.resume_action` (request.rs:240-241). This build
    logs no run request, so the field itself is inferred from the
    composition's action, one match arm away.

  * The composed history carried the call and its result, and the server
    read both. :7061-:7062 decomposed against history.rs's shapes — a
    system entry is `{"role":"system","content":"…"}`, 30 bytes of frame;
    user 53 and assistant 58 as probe 1 found; a step under 128 bytes is
    1+1+(1+1+len); a UserMessage is (1+len+text)+(1+1+36):

    root[0]  ce20faa643dd5597  170040  system head: 30 + 170,010 escaped —
                                       736 more than probe 1's; what
                                       differed between the two sessions'
                                       `request.system` is not in the log FETCHED :7065
    root[1]  b46f50b0bc02f7c8    1334  user: 53 + 1,281 escaped, of which
                                       the prompt is 167 (:7033) and the
                                       rest is the request-only text the
                                       engine joins onto the newest user
                                       message — see incidental           FETCHED :7066
    root[2]  7ab301a1e710b296     178  assistant: no text, one paragraph —
                                       `[Tool Call] bash ` (17) + a 97-byte
                                       compact `{"command":…}` = 114, +6
                                       for the six characters JSON escapes
                                       in it, +58                         FETCHED :7067
    root[3]  79e4836f6086f40e      71  `[Tool Result]`, newline, the 2-byte
                                       output: 53 + 18 (16 raw, its two
                                       newlines escaped)                  FETCHED :7064
    turns[0] 753f02de266bda9c     104  ConversationTurn: 1+1+(3 × (1+1+32))
                                       — the user_message id and two steps FETCHED :7063
    turn.user_message
             00e3b29d736b904e    1311  UserMessage: (1+2+1,270 text) +
                                       (1+1+36 derived message_id), the
                                       same joined text as root[1],
                                       unescaped                          FETCHED :7068
    step[0]  2098a677ac8c8cd6     118  the assistant paragraph in proto
                                       framing: 1+1+(1+1+114)             not fetched
    step[1]  0d68653ddbe2ec51      20  the result: 1+1+(1+1+16)           FETCHED :7071

    The sizes sum to 173,176 (:7061 bytes=); 173,058 was fetched in seven
    gets, 173,038 of it before the first thinking delta. Both root/step
    pairs close on each other and on nothing else: 178/118 only for an
    input that is exactly the plan's command under a lone `command` key
    (no description, no timeout — the six escapes are its four quotes and
    the doubled backslash), and 71/20 only for an output that is exactly
    the line count and its newline, which is what shell.rs:313 returns for
    a clean exit (stdout verbatim, no wrapper). So what the model sent and
    what the tool printed are both pinned by the arithmetic without a byte
    of either in the log. root[1]/user_message close the same way: 1,281
    escaped over 1,270 raw is 11 escapes — the prompt's newline and
    backslash, the join's two newlines, and the seven the `<deferred_tools>`
    listing carries (deferral.rs:232-240) — which says the listing was the
    only text joined on and the reminders were empty.

  * The tool ran exactly once, from three sides. The file: one line, by the
    user's own `! wc -l` after the turn (the re-execution check — a second
    call would have appended a second `run`). The transcript: one Tool
    part, Completed, then the reply (the TUI). The wire: one `bridging an
    exec` in the session (:7054); zero `partial_tool_call` and zero
    `tool_call_started` on B (:7060-:7085); zero holds on B. And zero
    `answering a bridged exec` lines in the whole session — the result
    never went back as an exec answer, because the body it would have gone
    out on was gone; it went out as root[3], the D553 shape, and a model
    shown the call it made beside the result it produced did not make the
    call again. That is the divergence history.rs:37-42 argues for,
    holding on one sample.

  * The reply was `1`, and the turn ended cleanly: step_completed at :7084,
    no error of any kind (the header), and the session's next line is the
    one-shot's composition.

  * This is the first recovered request the server has accepted — the
    first `resume_action` this build has sent it, over a history whose
    `[Tool Call]` and `[Tool Result]` entries it fetched (:7067, :7064) and
    answered from without a call.

Timings, composition to first thinking delta (the same two ends probe 1
measured, for the same reason — no text-delta, send or clean-end line):

Read carefully: B, which fetched 173 KB of state — every root entry, the
turn wrapper, its user message and its last step — reached its first
thinking 0.29 s *sooner* than A, which fetched nothing. One sample per arm
on Auto; as probe 1 said of its pair, not a measurement of the fetch's
cost. What it bounds: the batch of five gets was answered 1.2 s after the
request went out, the sixth 1.6 s after that, and the model was thinking
5.4 s after the last of those — B's 8.2 s went to the model, not to the
fetch.

Fetch order, against probe 1's: turns[0], the LAST root entry, then
root[0] onward in order — probe 1 saw turns[0], root[5], root[0..4]; this
saw turns[0], root[3], root[0..2]. Two recordings, one order. Then, new
here: the turn's user_message 1.56 s later on its own, and the turn's last
step at the instant the model started — two blobs inside the turn wrapper
that probe 1's `action="user"` request never saw dereferenced. Probe 1's
item 5 ("does not prove the server has no path that would") now has the
path: a resume reads into the wrapper, for the user message and the last
step, and — on this sample — not for the assistant step between them.

Reading checklist (C-M5, C-M1'):

  * A get for an id this build never minted: NO. All seven gets name ids
    in the :7062 listing; one composed id (step[0], 118) was never asked
    for; no asked-for id was uncomposed, and none went unanswered-found.

  * Either `message_id` echoed anywhere visible: NOT DETERMINABLE, as
    probe 1 — a case-sensitive grep of the session for `message_id` and
    `conversation_id` returns nothing. The one server-minted id shown is
    :7054's call id, index 0 on a first exec, the shape probe 1 records.

  * Anything attributable to `conversation_id`: NOTHING SEPARABLE. A and B
    carried the same derived value (history.rs:501, from messages[0]); C
    carried its own. The one difference between the three Runs with two
    candidate causes is under incidental.

== P4 — the checkpoint arm on a bridged turn ==
VERDICT: YES — it arrives on the recovered Run and on the one-shot: 6
arrivals, n from 483 to 3249; none on the Run that was dropped

`unmodelled server-message fields provider="cursor" fields=[(3, n)]`:

  A   none                                                    0 arrivals
  B   :7081 (3, 1353)  :7083 (3, 521)   :7085 (3, 521)        3 arrivals
  C   :7260 (3, 3249)  :7262 (3, 483)   :7264 (3, 483)        3 arrivals

Placement is probe 1's exactly: on each Run that finished, one arrives
after the kv-set burst (:7081 after :7078-:7080; :7260 after :7256-:7259)
and the run's last two are a pair of identical size bracketing
`step_completed (17)` (:7084 between the two 521s; :7263 between the two
483s). A had no tool_call_completed and no set burst after its hold — its
server never reached the point probe 1's first arrival came at — so "on a
bridged turn" here means the *recovered* request of one: the arm is not
tied to the Run that made the call, and a turn whose held Run is dropped
still gets its checkpoints on the Run that finishes it. Only the size is
seen; the arm is not decoded.

The `token_details` bead's first step is: model the arm.

== P5 — `conversation_id` (5): sent, reference parity ==
Sent on all three Runs, the value derived from `messages[0]`'s id
(history.rs:501): the same on A and B, C's own on C. Nothing came back
naming it (checklist above), so whether it matters is not observable from
this client, as the plan states. Nothing new measured.

== P6 — `pre_fetched_blobs` (17): not sent ==
Not sent; the shipped client never fills it, so it is unmeasured at both
ends. What would justify it is B's own numbers above — six gets, 173 KB,
all answered by +2.8 s against a first thinking delta at +8.2 s — and on
this sample the gets were not what the model waited on.

== what this cannot measure ==

1. One drop reason live: `Idle`. `Closed` is the e2e suite's (AC-16, over
   the testkit's `Hangup`); `Cancelled` and `Evicted` have their sentences
   pinned by unit test (AC-14) and have never been recovered from against
   the real server.

2. The cap's `Failed` arm was not reached — by design: a second drop of
   this key did not occur, and nothing here says what the server does
   with a second `resume_action` over the same conversation. AC-14b and
   AC-16b own it, against the mock.

3. One seat, one account, Auto on all three Runs, one client version, one
   afternoon; one turn of history, one call, one result of two bytes. A
   named model, a multi-call step, a result at the tool's clamp, or a
   `[Tool Call]` at CALL_INPUT_LIMIT (clamped_calls=0 again) is
   unmeasured.

4. Nothing about a Run that dies *during* generation. A was idle-held with
   its answer outstanding when it was dropped; a body that closes under a
   delta or under a partial_tool_call leaves a different transcript
   (`Pending`/`Running` rendered as NO_RESULT, history.rs:342-345) and was
   not exercised.

5. Whether the server *used* what it newly fetched. That the turn's
   user_message (:7068) and last step (:7071) were dereferenced on a
   resume — where probe 1's user-action request left them alone — is
   observed; whether they reached the model, fed a checkpoint, or were
   read and dropped is not. The same for the one it did not fetch: one
   sample says the assistant step is not read on a resume, and does not
   say it never is.

6. Where the server's hold ceiling is. `Idle` bounds it from below at
   600 s under 5 s heartbeats; a resume on the body at 599 s, or a hold
   past 600 s, is unmeasured, and IDLE_BOUND's own doc (bridge.rs:120-129)
   says it is a backstop, not a guess at the ceiling.

7. First-*text*-delta timing, the run request's send instant, the
   heartbeats, and the clean EndStream: none has a log line, as probe 1's
   item 7.

8. What (3, n) carries, and whether A's server would ever have produced
   one — A was dropped before the point probe 1's first arrival came at.

9. Whether the request-only text in root[1] (incidental) changes anything
   the model does on a resumed history: not separable from anything else
   here.

== incidental, and worth knowing before W4 ==

* The newest user message's root entry carries text the transcript does
  not hold. root[1] is 1,334 bytes for a 167-byte prompt: the engine
  appends its reminders and the per-step `<deferred_tools>` listing to the
  request's newest user message as text parts (session.rs:3379-3403, "the
  REQUEST and not the transcript"), and `entries()` joins every text part
  of a message (history.rs:242). Two consequences the arithmetic makes
  visible. The turn's user_message blob (1311) carries the same joined
  text, so both blobs of that message hash over the deferral state at the
  step they were composed at — an activation between two steps re-mints
  both ids, where history.rs:20-22 expects a rebuild to yield the same
  ones; not exercised here (nothing activated), an inference from the
  source the sizes agree with. And a resumed session's history carries the
  listing as it stood when that message was newest — a fact about the
  request, not the transcript, and one probe 1 could not see: its headless
  runs built their requests before an MCP server had connected (zero
  deferral lines in either window), so their user entries were the prompt
  alone.

* The no-history request's large server set scales with the request. A's
  server set 191,609 bytes at :7042 (probe 1's R1: 190,884), 2.5 s in; C —
  also entries=0 — got 15,612 and 12,749 (:7089, :7088); B, with a root
  supplied, nothing above 1,078 (:7082). Probe 1's two candidate causes
  for the absence on a rooted request both still fit (C's derived id was
  as new to the server as A's); what is new is that the size on the two
  unrooted requests differs by 12×, and the one thing known to differ
  between them from this side is the request's own system text and
  prompt. Which of those it follows is not measured.

* The one-shot is sent from the TUI: nine kv sets (:7088-:7091,
  :7256-:7259, :7261), 86 thinking deltas, its own three (3, n) arrivals
  and its own step_completed at :7263 — 3.29 s. Probe 1's `ganja run`
  composed it at teardown and never sent it. Same wire, different
  frontend lifetime.

* Server-minted per-step call ids, again: :7054's `call-<v4>-0` over
  `fc_<hex>_0`, index 0 on a first exec — probe 1 saw -0/-1 and -2 across
  two steps. B minted none: no exec.

* kv sets in the session: 7 on A, 4 on B, 9 on C, 20 in all; 168 is the
  whole day's log (148 at probe 1's writing, +20). `a server set replaced
  bytes this run already held`: zero in the session, still zero in the
  file.

* The hold's own lines are two, 52.6 ms apart (:7054 bridging, :7058
  holding), and the heartbeat between them and the drop is silent: a
  reader of this log will see ten minutes of nothing between :7058 and
  :7059, and that silence is the shipped keeper doing what its doc says.

* `field 25` beside partial_tool_call and tool_call_started (:7051,
  :7053): unchanged from probe 1, on the one exec.
